batch_notes: go/bubbles is 24 properties of one shape: a mirror/model written in the test, driven by random op sequences with a check after every step (15 stateful-model); the few single-shot ones (help layout, progress bar, placeholder, LineInfo, wrapped view) are model-oracle, and two compare the real cursor with the virtual one (internal-consistency). Several bubbles 'models' lean on library internals (the textarea wrap grid, the textinput window offsets, the library's own window arithmetic in filepicker/tree), so model-oracle vs internal-consistency is blurry there. Attribution: the bubbles README states plainly that most bugs (roughly 60 of 97) were seen on reading the source and only confirmed/gated by the properties; only about 20 are said to have been found by a property. Per the rubric's rule 2 (property text cites the id / gates it) these are 'explicit', so the explicit count overstates property-found bugs badly; each note says which. The rubric does not distinguish 'cites as gated' (property would fail, counts the shape) from 'cites as avoided' (generator steers around it: bubbles/54, /91, cast/1, /2); I marked both explicit but flagged the avoided ones. Many bubbles properties count pinned shapes with zootest.Count and carry on instead of failing, a 'gate by cause' pattern that lets one property carry 5-8 bug ids. go/cast quality issue: bug ids in test comments are misnumbered (TestHegelMapsConvertValueWise says 'pinned, cast/5' for the cast/7 swallow; TestHegelIntegersAreUnixSeconds says 'pinned (cast/7)' for cast/9), which pollutes mentioned_by for cast/5 and cast/7. No pin-tagged properties in this batch. Interesting: filepicker over real temp-dir trees, the timer/stopwatch/spinner mirrors of tea.Cmd tick chains in flight, cell-by-cell SGR colour checks of the progress bar, and a spring-convergence property.
